oembed.title: ✨8 must try places to eat in Lisbon Portugal 🇵🇹 📍Among the many amazing things to do in Lisbon, eating is one of them! Save this list of incredible hidden gems, local eats, and beautiful Lisbon restaurants & dining experiences. #lisbonfood #lisbonfoodie #lisbonrestaurant #lisbonportugal #creatorsearchinsights

videos.transcript: If you're visiting Lisbon, save this because I'm sharing eight unreal places to eat, including where to eat like a king for under €5 at the end. Up first, Solada de Medela for authentic bifana. Soft crusty bun, juicy pork, simple but so tasty. Too fast for real. From modern elevated Portuguese classic, the fava beans with ribs, sauteed shrimp and truffle and egg, all flavor bombs had chocolate mousse, rich, nutty and decadent. 3 Gelataria Laverde, our favorite gelato in Lisbon. Super creamy, creative flavors like Dubai Chocolate and pist del Dinata. And now they even have gelato burgers. For Parrillo Wine Bistro, not only did they have an amazing wine selection, every dish blew me away. The beef tartare was perfectly seasoned and silky. That allantation, black pork, bold, smoky and super tender, ending with the caramel cream perfection. 5 Omamariscara. Seafood lovers, this one's for you. It's seafood rice is legendary, like a creamy risotto packed with generous amounts of fresh seafood. End with a shot of ginjinha. 6, Arca Bistro for modern European cuisine. Unique flavor combinations. That piri piri chicken had such a nice spiciness. And love that creamy tziki Bas cheesecake. Unreal. 7 Marandina da Arco Benderra, local gem with massive grilled sardines and clams in a garlic herb oil. Huge portion, super authentic. 8 Confiteria Nacional. They eat like a king. Try bologra or my go to Bolog, the Berlin.

The reason that are traditional kind of tapas restaurants in Portugal. Restaurante picapau. Food here is also fantastic. You need to get the mussels. So the picapau chicken is also fantastic. oembed.title: The perfect 3-day itinerary for your first trip to Mexico City 🌿 *please forgive my pronunciation!!* Is this be a packed trip? Yes. Are there MANY more incredible local spots & things to do? Absolutely. But each one of these spots is worth a visit and this is how you can plan it out to make the most of your short time ✨ #mexicocity #visitmexico #cdmx

videos.transcript: Here's how I would spend three days on your first trip to Mexico City. It feels like there's a million recommendations for Mexico City these days, which can make trip planning feel really overwhelming. here's how I'd map out three days to hit some of the city's top spots. Is it a little touristy? Yes, but there's a reason these places are so popular, and this itinerary lets you see a lot of them in a short amount of time. Start your first day early with coffee and pastries. If you want to see what all the hype is about, definitely head to Panaderia Rosetta. But get there early cause the line does get long. I do think it's worth it to try at least once. Their pastries are delicious in my opinion, and the famous guava roll lived up to the hype. But this is definitely not your only option. There are so many incredible bakeries and cafes all over the city. Since you'll be in Roma Norte, you can just wander around for a bit. I think this is one of the prettiest neighborhoods. Walk through El Parian. This is the beautiful interiors you see here. There are little shops, another coffee shop, and then make your way to Jenny's quesadillas. Let's call this your late morning snack or early lunch. But heads up, you do need cash here. Stroll through Park a Mexico, and then you'll be in the beautiful Condesa neighborhood with more in the afternoon, take A short Uber ride up to Chapultepec Castle entry cost about $10 and I think it's absolutely worth it to walk around. The grounds are so beautiful. You can see inside and then a great overview of the entire city. After freshening up a bit, head to micompachava or conchamar for dinner and then Balter Bar after for drinks. Okay. For day two you have two options. Option one is a full day trip to Grutas Tolantongo. We left the city at 4:00am and we got back at four PM, so it's absolutely doable in one day. It is a very long day, but I thought it was completely worth it. We started in these beautiful hot springs, got a bit of breakfast, then headed over to this waterfall, swim around, then ended the day at the natural river. It didn't feel crowded at the times we went, so I really recommend going with a tour. Who knows the best times to go? I would plan a more casual dinner that night, just grabbing tacos at a local spot. Your second option for day two is a shorter day trip that's just about 45 minutes outside of the city. I would still probably leave early in the morning so you can try to miss the afternoon traffic on the way back. For this one, you'll start at the Frida Kahlo Museum, then wander through the Coyocan market, and then head to Sochi Moco to spend the afternoon on one of The colourful boats which are usually all you can drink and turn into a little party. I'd book a later dinner this day somewhere like Martinez Lardo or Quintonil. I've linked both these experiences in my bio if you want to see the exact ones. I recommend start day three with a quick breakfast somewhere like Cafe Milao and then drive 45 minutes out to T O T. Walk on this is where you can do the famous hot air balloon ride, which if you're doing that, you're actually gonna start way earlier cause they're usually at sunrise. Otherwise you can just walk around the pyramids and learn a bit of the history. After that, drive just a few minutes over to have lunch at LA Gruta. Okay, this may not be the best meal you'll have in Mexico City, but I do think it's worth it for the ambience. You're eating in a cave, it's very cool and you can't go wrong with some drinks and chips and guac. And head back into the city. And I would keep the afternoon pretty flexible depending on how much you wanna do. You could do any last minute shopping, go check out the famous library for their architecture, or head to the National Museum of anthropology for your final dinner. I love to set. And then you can walk 20 ish minutes or drive about eight minutes to either handshake speak easy or hanky panky. Handshake often gets ranked as No. 1 On multiple lists. I actually prefer hanky panky. Both are amazing. Definitely make reservations. And since you'll immediately want to book a trip back to Mexico City, I would say next time plan to have some more downtime and try some of the local spots. oembed.title: 5 restaurants we’d genuinely recommend in Lisbon 🇵🇹 🍷  Save this food guide for your trip 📌  Wondering where to eat in Lisbon? We spent 3 months living in the city, eating our way through countless restaurants. These are the 5 we’d happily return to 👇 📍Antiga @antigawinebar  🍽️ Modern Portuguese petiscos (Portugal’s answer to tapas) 🥩 Order the Pork Belly & Duck Confit 🍷 Fantastic regional Portuguese wines – ask the staff for a pairing recommendation. 📍Le 17.45 @le17.45  🧀 Build your own cheese & charcuterie board by ticking your favourites from the menu. The staff are also brilliant at helping you choose. ⭐ Don’t miss the award-winning Portuguese cheeses, French artisan cheeses & Chouriço Assado. 📍Santelmo @santelmolisboa  🐙 Modern Portuguese seafood with a seasonal menu. 🍷 We kicked things off with a natural wine from Portugal’s Douro Valley. 🦐 Order the Garlic Butter Prawns & Octopus (and definitely get bread to soak up all the sauce!) 📍Intenso @intenso_lx  ✨ Contemporary Portuguese cuisine inspired by traditional recipes. 🥩 Our favourite dish was their take on Pica-Pau. 🍫 Finish with the Chocolate Surprise – a white chocolate mousse sphere with a Ginja (Portuguese liqueur) centre, topped with warm 70% chocolate. 📍Cantinho do Aziz @cantinhodoazizstore  🇲🇿 One of Lisbon’s best family-run Mozambican restaurants. 🥟 Start with the Samosas. 🍛 We love the Piripiri Lamb Bakra & Goat Chacuti. It’s become a tradition for us to eat here every time we’re in Lisbon. 👉 Most of these are popular dinner spots, so we’d recommend booking ahead – especially during summer. 🗺️ Want even more Lisbon food recommendations? Our interactive Lisbon Food Map includes 40+ food spots – Link in our bio. 📌 Save this guide for your Lisbon foodie trip.  #lisbonfood #lisbonrestaurants #wheretoeatinlisbon #lisbontravel #portugalfood

videos.transcript: We spent three months living here and eating our way through the city and these are five restaurants we genuinely recommend. Welcome to Lisbon, one of our favourite foodie cities. First up, we have Antigua Wine Bar. We actually found this place by accident and ended up being one of our favourite discoveries. It takes traditional Portuguese flavours and gives them a modern twist. You need to try the corn fed duck leg and crispy. Next up, if you love cheese and wine, you have to visit this place. Instead of ordering from a normal menu, they give you a checklist where you can build your own charcuterie board alongside a little guidebook explaining each cheese. From truffle cheese and French classics to award winning Portuguese cheeses and beautifully cured meats. You could honestly spend hours here drinking Portuguese wine and eating the best cheese you've ever had. Next up is Santelmo, a modern Portuguese restaurant. We kick things off with a natural wine from Portugal's Douro Valley. The tuna croquettes were so flavourful. Prawns arrived swimming in a rich garlic butter sauce. They're also very well known for their grilled octopus. And then finishing off with a super light, creamy cheesecake. Then we have intenso, a trendy, highly rated port. These restaurants in central Lisbon, known for its modern spin on Portuguese classics. The pica pica was my absolute favourite dish. It was so rich. They take seasonal Portuguese ingredient and turn them into beautifully refined dishes without over Complicating them. And then our final stop is proof that Lisbon's food scene is so much more than just Portuguese cuisine. Thanks to Portugal's history with Mozambique, this city is home to some incredible mozambiquean restaurants. And this family run spot has become very popular. We've been here three times and the lamb bakar is still my favourite dish. It's very different to the rest of the list. And that's exactly why we think you should visit. Save this for your trip to Lisbon.

videos.transcript: This is all the best food I ate on my trip to Tokyo, Japan, one of the most epic food cities in the world. First up we have these insane viral cream stuffed sandwiches in fried Japanese milk bread from age 3. Next, the table side sizzling three cheese bison burger from American Diner. Then we got this third thin stack of pancakes that comes with a whole stick of homemade butter. Next up, and one of my favorites, this huge unagi bowl from Izumo. Then we got this thick cut Japanese milk bread French toast in a pool of honey butter from the front room. Next we hit the famous Kijiji Fish Market, known for their insanely fresh sushi, all kinds of seafood, and tons of traditional Japanese dishes you can try while roaming the market. Then we went to Benizuru for their famous souffle pancakes that you can customize and they cook and prepare right in front of you. Next we have the viral carbonara udon topped with Parmesan cut bacon from mentaishy. Then we tried one of the famous salmon ro bowls where they put on a show with this giant bowl of salmon eggs. Next we got 7 11, maybe the most popular spot in Japan. We got their famous egg salad and so many other crazy snacks I never knew existed. Then we got Genza Huchigo, a six seat Michelin starred ramen spot run by arguably the cutest Japanese chef in all of Tokyo. We Also tried one of the only Texas style barbecue spots in Japan and serving up this colossal beef rib. Next I did Yoshi's nine hundred dollar omakase experience. A fourth generation sushi master that cooks for you in his own home. And last up, and easily the most insane dining experience from the trip at Wagyu Mafia. If you wanna see everything I ate on my trip, it's live on YouTube right now. Check it out. Link in bio.

oembed.title: 5 FOOD SPOTS IN TOKYO JAPAN 🇯🇵 🍜 Menchirashi - viral carbonara udon for less than £5 a bowl 🍚 Ginza Tonkatsu Saito -  crispiest, juiciest pork cutlets with shredded cabbage, rice & miso soup  🍗 Oreryū Shio Ramen - rich, comforting bowls of noodles topped with pork belly and fried chicken  🥩 Niku to Tamago - omurice served on sizzling hot plates with hamburger, cheese and curry sauce   🐟Tonkatsu Akira - rare salmon katsu with unlimited sticky rice Follow for more Tokyo recommendations! ✨ #tokyo #japan #tokyofood #tokyorestaurants #japanfood

videos.transcript: Here are five food spots you need to try in Tokyo. First up is Menchirashi where you can get the viral carbonara udon the noodles are made fresh right in front of you and it's creamy, delicious and for less than £5 a bowl it's definitely worth the hype. Next, check out Ginza Tonkatsu Saito head downstairs for the crispiest tonkatsu you'll have in Tokyo you'll get a juicy pork cutlet shredded cabbage, rice and miso soup and trust me you're not gonna want to miss it. Head over to Oreryu Shio Ramen for huge portions of super rich comforting bowls of noodles topped with crispy fried chicken this is a must try and they've got multiple restaurants across Tokyo. For omurice, visit Niku to Tamago which quite literally translates to meat and egg you'll get a sizzling hot plate with a hamburger, omelette rice and curry sauce. You have to stop by Tonkatsu Akira for the rare salmon katsu the salmon is super silky and delicious and you get unlimited sticky rice. Make sure you save this post and follow for more Tokyo recommendations.

videos.transcript: Here are the top five New York City restaurants of 2026, based on 40 million ratings. This year on belly. At No. 5 is Marcel, one of the most stunning restaurants in the city. We love their onion soup, steak o papov, and giant chocolate mousse. I rank them at a 9.1 on my belly list. No. 4 is Odo East Village, this olacart sequel to the two Michelin starred. Odo allows you to build your own kaiseki. Our favorite dish was their braised wagyu beef tongue with red wine reduction and Parmesan. No. 3 is Kidilum, one of the best new Indian restaurants in the city. We're obsessed with their flaky paratha, Paul curry, nandu curry, and the kalanjhi. Gave them a 9.7 on belly. No. 2 is Ambassadors Clubhouse, the New York location of one of London's top rated Indian restaurants. Some of our favorite dishes are their signature butter chicken chops, the lamb biryani, and their lamb chops. I gave them a 9.8. And finally, at No. 1 is aresh, from the superstar group behind the corner store in the 86 and the former executive chef of the Michelin star schmone. We love their bluefin tuna crudo, halloumi, Jerusalem bagel, short rib, and their cardamom soft serve. I gave them a 9.7 on belly.

oembed.title: Most "best restaurants in Lisbon" lists are written for tourists. This one isn't. One spot for breakfast, lunch and dinner, each earning its place, not just photogenic. Truffle croque madame at Alba, aperitivo-style lunch (and a resident corgi) at Polpetta Cosmica, Georgian khinkali with black truffle at Karater. Where to eat in Lisbon like you actually live there. Full list linked in bio. #Lisbon #WhereToEatLisbon #LisbonRestaurants #MoveToLisbon #ExpatLife

videos.transcript: Where to eat in Lisbon breakfast, lunch and dinner from someone who's been living here for five years, part 1. If you're only doing breakfast once in Lisbon, make it at home Cafe. They somehow always manage to reinvent the classics. Whether there's a blueberry matcha or a creme brulee French toast, everything feels really thought through and the quality is consistently great. For lunch, I'll go to Poppetta Cosmica. Imagine the feeling of an Italian aperitivo, but in the middle of the day. Good food, good wine, good music, and a cozy space where people actually slow down, share plates, and stay for a while. The lasagna and focaccia are generally the best I've had in Lisbon. They also have the cutest corgi wandering around, which makes the experience even better. If I ever owned an Italian cafe, this is how I would want it to look like. For dinner, I'm heading to fabric. It's a Middle Eastern restaurant right on Huajin Zhongpu and it's become my go to Friday night spot. The portions are generous and every dish has so many different flavours and textures that makes you appreciate each bite. Follow for part two!
